name: Tractors & Machinery Systems

objectives.text: Identify the major systems of a farm tractor, including the engine, drivetrain, hydraulic system, electrical system, and operator station
Identify common farm implements used for tillage, planting, spraying, haying, and harvesting and match each to the field task it performs
Explain the meaning of the safety decals, warning symbols, and operator control symbols found on tractors and implements
Describe the items on a daily pre-operation walk-around inspection checklist for a tractor and explain why each is checked
Explain the function of the power take-off (PTO) and the entanglement hazards it presents along with the shielding that guards against them
Explain how a rollover protective structure (ROPS) and seat belt protect the operator and identify conditions that cause tractor rollovers and runovers
Explain how the clutch, transmission, differential, and final drive transfer power from the engine to the drive wheels
Demonstrate the correct procedure for attaching, leveling, and adjusting a three-point hitch implement and connecting a PTO driveline
Perform a pre-operation inspection, start-up, and shut-down of a tractor following the operator's manual
Summarize safe practices for transporting tractors and implements on public roads, including SMV emblems, lighting, safety chains, and transport locks
Operate a tractor safely through a driving course that includes hitching a drawbar implement, maneuvering, and backing a trailer
Compare two-wheel drive, mechanical front-wheel drive, four-wheel drive, and tracked tractors in terms of traction, soil compaction, and suitable field uses
Calculate the ballast, tire inflation pressure, and drawbar horsepower needed to safely and efficiently pull a given implement
Calibrate a sprayer, planter, or grain drill to apply a target rate and adjust settings to correct the application
Calculate power transmission efficiency from engine to PTO and drawbar using speed, torque, and horsepower measurements
Calculate theoretical field capacity, actual field capacity, and field efficiency for a tractor and implement combination
Explain how GPS guidance, auto-steer, ISOBUS, and section or rate control integrate with tractor and implement systems to improve precision
Calculate the hourly and per-acre ownership and operating costs of a tractor and implement, including depreciation, interest, fuel, repairs, and labor
Analyze whether purchasing, leasing, or custom hiring a tractor and implements would best serve a farm business or SAE operation
Evaluate a tractor and implement system's sizing and suitability for a given field task and justify the equipment selection
Design an operator safety and training plan for the tractors and machinery used in a farm or SAE operation

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording the grade 5 systems, grade 7 PTO, grade 8 hitch, and grade 12 selection objectives for precision. Split pre-operation inspection into describing it at grade 6 and performing it at grade 9. Added safety decals, ROPS and rollovers, drivetrain power flow, implement identification, road transport, a tractor driving course, drive type comparison, implement calibration, power transmission efficiency, field capacity, precision ag integration, machinery costs, the purchase, lease, or custom hire decision, and an operator safety plan. Troubleshooting, electrical service, engine work, hydraulics, and routine maintenance are left to the sibling sub-topics.
